record.paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
record.original_question: Let z(N0) be a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal, and let S− be the backward shift on z(N0). Determine whether case 4 from Section 2.1 can occur; that is, determine whether the range M(I − 2S−|z) can be closed and have infinite codimension.

evidence.quote: 4. M(I − 2S−|z) is closed and cod ( M(I − 2S−|z) ) = ∞.

The preceding considerations lead to a rough classification of quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals. The cases 1, 2, and 5 actually occur, while cases 3 and 4 are questionable; see Problems 1 and 2.
Problem 2. Find out whether case 4 is impossible.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. Let $\mathbb{N}_0=\{0,1,2,\dots\}$ and let $\omega(\mathbb{N}_0)$ denote the linear space of all scalar sequences $x=(\xi_0,\xi_1,\xi_2,\dots)$. A linear subspace $\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)\subseteq\omega(\mathbb{N}_0)$ equipped with a quasi-norm $\|\cdot\mid\mathfrak{z}\|$ is called a quasi-Banach sequence ideal if it is complete and if, whenever $x\in\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ and $y\in\omega(\mathbb{N}_0)$ satisfy $|\eta_k|\le|\xi_k|$ for all $k$, one has $y\in\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ with $\|y\mid\mathfrak{z}\|\le\|x\mid\mathfrak{z}\|$.

The forward shift $S_+$ and backward shift $S_-$ act on $\omega(\mathbb{N}_0)$ by
$$S_+(\xi_0,\xi_1,\xi_2,\dots)=(0,\xi_0,\xi_1,\dots),\qquad S_-(\xi_0,\xi_1,\xi_2,\dots)=(\xi_1,\xi_2,\xi_3,\dots).$$
The quasi-Banach sequence ideal $\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is called shift-monotone if both $S_+$ and $S_-$ map $\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ continuously into itself.

For a continuous linear operator $T:\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)\to\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)$, denote by $M(T)$ its range. Consider the operator $I-2S_-$ acting on $\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)$, and its range $M(I-2S_-\mid\mathfrak{z})$.

Question. Does there exist a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal $\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ such that the range $M(I-2S_-\mid\mathfrak{z})$ is closed in $\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ and has infinite codimension? Equivalently, can this case occur, or is it impossible?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem (Problem 2) in a 2023 work on traces on operator ideals over Banach spaces. A web search did not turn up any subsequent paper resolving whether the range of $I-2S_-$ on a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal can be closed and of infinite codimension. No solution appears to be available as of the search date.

status_evidence.title: The Spectrum of Shift Operators and the Existence of Traces
status_evidence.snippet: Studies spectra of forward/backward shifts on shift-monotone sequence ideals and their relation to traces, providing the framework for the classification leading to cases 1–5.
status_evidence.claim: Provides background framework but does not resolve case 4.
